Tshirt Workshop · Staff guide

Graphic Engine

Graphic Engine gets artwork ready to print. Open a design, tell it the print size, choose how it prints, check it, save it. Most jobs take four clicks.

Open it from the Workshop Board board.tshirtworkshop.com.au/engine Sign in to the board first. Your art stays on this computer. The one exception is Check with Claude in Batch, which sends a small picture of each result to be looked over.
  1. Open a design
  2. Set the print size
  3. Choose how it prints
  4. Speed buttons and Presets
  5. Look it over

The screen at a glance

  • 1The top bar. File name, print size and a sharpness badge on the left. Undo, Redo, Batch, Sheet, More, Open art and Save PNG on the right.
  • 2Tabs. Each design you open gets its own tab. An amber dot means it isn’t saved yet. A green tick means it is.
  • 3The tool row. Crop, Select, the views, and Ink. A button with a small arrow opens a short list.
  • 4Before on the left, After on the right. The dashed line is the edge of the print.
  • 5Zoom. Fit, Life size, more zoom levels, and a button you hold to flick back to the original.
  • 6Three steps. Print size, Print style, Check & save. One shows at a time. Click a box to jump to it.
  • 7This design. A small picture of the print, the shirt colour behind it, and a way to try the design two ways.

Under the steps are Speed buttons, Fine-tune, Presets and History. The tool is dark so colours are easy to judge, like Photoshop. More at the top has Light mode, Full screen and this guide. The Tools tab on the edge of the panel folds the panel away for more room.

1

Open a design

The tool opens on a start screen that asks what you’re making.

Drop the art, or click to choose itOne file, a few files, or a zip of a whole order. PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF and SVG all open. You can also paste a picture.
Get one design readyThe everyday job. Set the size, pick a look, save a print-ready PNG.
Do a whole orderLots of files at once, like names and numbers. This opens Batch.
Just tidy a fileRemove a background or flatten colours for tracing. No dots.
Practise on the sample artNo file handy? This loads a made-up design to try things on.

From the Workshop Board

On a job on the board, Open in Graphic Engine sends the art straight here, with the order number and placement already filled in for the file name. A whole order can be sent to Batch the same way, and it arrives already sorted into its groups. If Batch happens to be showing when one design arrives, it steps aside so you see the design straight away.

Once a design is open, Open art at the top opens another in a new tab.

2

Set the print size

  1. Step 1 asks How wide is the print? Click Chest 90, Front 280, Back 330 or Largest.
  2. Or set your own: use − and +, drag the slider, or type the width or the height in mm. The other follows.
  3. Look at the green or amber line under it. Green means the file is sharp enough at that size.
  4. Click Done · next.

Always set the size first. Everything is worked out at the real print size. If you change the size later, the tool redraws, which is fine. What you must never do is resize a saved file in another program. Any dots would change size with it.

The largest print is 400 × 500 mm, either way round. The tool won’t go past it.

What the tool tells you here

“No size is saved in this file”The file doesn’t know how big it should print. Choose a width. Until you do, the check list keeps reminding you.
“Upscale needed”The file is too small for that size and will print soft. The note says how much to enlarge it, or how wide it can print as it is. If it’s far too small, ask the customer for a bigger file or vector art.
“There’s empty space around the art”Click Trim to the art. The size then measures the design, not the blank margin.
3

Choose how it prints

DTF film can’t print ink that is half see-through. Every spot is either solid ink or clear film. So soft shading (a glow, a shadow, a fade) has to become one of two things: a clean hard edge, or tiny solid dots. Step 2 asks How should it print? and gives four print styles.

Clean cut

Solid ink, no dots

For logos, lettering, bold art and normal pictures. Soft edges print fully solid or are removed, so the outline is crisp. The tool starts here.

Halftone

Shading becomes dots

For photos, glows, smoke, flames and anything that fades into the shirt. Tiny solid dots that look like shading from arm’s length.

Trace prep

Flat colours for tracing

Not a print file. It flattens a logo into clean flat colours so Illustrator’s Image Trace gives tidy shapes. See step 12.

DTG

Solid background, nothing removed

For jobs going on the DTG printer. A solid colour fills the box behind the art, and the DTG software knocks the shirt colour out when it prints.

Then a Quick start

Under the print styles is a Quick start. Pick the closest one and watch the After side.

Clean cutRemove shadows: a quick clean-up for dark shirts. Shadows drop out and the rest prints solid.
Knock out the shirt colour: colours close to the shirt colour drop out. This is the one the tool starts on.
Remove the background: for art on a plain backdrop, like a JPG logo on white.
Nothing removed (prep only): for art that is already print-ready and only needs sizing or a tidy.
HalftoneShadows to dots: only the deepest shadows turn into dots. Colours stay strong.
Fix soft edges: only glows, soft shadows and fades turn into dots. Solid parts stay solid.
Shirt shows through: colours close to the shirt drop out, and shading turns into dots. Lighter to wear.
Full halftone: the whole design becomes dots, for a soft vintage look.

Then Quick adjust

The pink box holds two or three sliders that matter most for the Quick start you chose, such as Soft edges and Specks cleared up to in Clean cut. Drag one and watch the After side. Hover over a slider to see what it does. Reset to defaults puts them back.

Set the Shirt colour first (in the This design box). Several Quick starts work from it.

“Better as DTG?”

Sometimes a small blue box appears under the print styles. The tool has measured a lot of soft glow, or a lot of ink for the print’s size, and thinks the job may suit DTG better. It’s a suggestion only. Click it to switch to DTG, or close it with the cross and it stays closed for that design.

DTG, in short

Choose DTG, then the Background colour: The shirt colour, Black, White or your own. Nothing is removed and there are no dots. Size, crop, sharpen, brightness and levels all still work. The file name gets _dtg.

Still new DTG files have not been through a full run on our DTG software yet. Check the first few on the printer before trusting it for a big job.
4

Speed buttons and Presets

This is the quick way in. One click sets the print style, the Quick start and the dots for an everyday job, then takes you to Check & save. Check the print size after.

Speed buttons

They sit under the three steps, on two tabs.

Built inQuick clean cut, Black tee, White tee, Coloured tee, Dark photo on black, Glows & soft shadows. The same on every computer.
OursSix spaces for the workshop’s own buttons. Set a job up the way you like, then click + Add on an empty one and name it.

Quick clean cut does three jobs at once: Clean cut with a hard edge, the background removed, and the file trimmed to the art. It’s the fastest way to prep a logo.

Presets

Open Presets, near the bottom of the panel, and choose from the list. To keep a set-up you like, click Save new and name it. Share with all computers sends it to the others. Sharing asks for the team code once on each computer. It’s in the Settings tab of the “DTF Halftone Presets” Google Sheet.

The list only shows presets for the print style you’re in. The built-in Starters and the Claude recipes are Halftone set-ups, so they show when Halftone is chosen.

Treat halftone set-ups as a starting point Most Starters and recipes were tuned on screen and have not been through a real print and wash yet. For a big or fussy job, print a small test first. The dot sizes come from the Dot limits buttons in Ink density, and there’s a test chart linked there to check them on our printer and film.
5

Look it over

The views

On shirtThe print on the shirt colour.
TransparentThe print on checks. The checks are clear film, so you can see every bit that was removed.
On a colourThe print over any solid colour, to check edges. A colour box and six swatches appear under the button. This doesn’t change the shirt colour or the print.
SplitTwo views side by side. They zoom and move together. Each side has a menu to choose what it shows.
Other viewsWhite base shows where the white ink goes under the colour. Ink map shows solid ink, dots, and what was removed. Print edge turns the dashed outline on or off.

Zoom

  • Fit shows the whole print. Life size shows it at its real size on your screen. The first time, click Set it up and match the box to a bank card. Do that once on each screen.
  • Zoom has 1:1, 2× and 4×. Look at 1:1 before every save. The Fit view can show patterns that aren’t really in the file.
  • When you’re zoomed in, a small map appears top right. The pink box is the part on screen. Click or drag in it to move around.
  • Hold Hold: Original to flick back to the art as it came in.

The shirt colour

In the This design box, click Change beside Shirt. Pick a swatch, use the Colour picker, or type a colour code. The eye button hides the shirt so you see the print on clear film.

Try it two ways

Not sure between Clean cut and Halftone? Click Try another way. The design as it stands is kept as A, and you carry on with a copy, B. Click A or B to flick between them. Side by side shows two versions in Split. The version showing is the one that saves. You can keep up to six.

6

Check and save

Read the check list

Step 3 is Check it, then save. Each line is a check the tool has done for you.

✓ Green tickGood. Nothing to do.
! Amber markRead it. It says what’s wrong and where to fix it. The step box shows how many there are, like “1 to check”.
Grey symbolJust telling you what was done, like “Background removed” or “Ink area down 50%”.

Name the file

Type the order number and placement in Order and placement, like 57615, full front. Jobs opened from the board have this filled in already.

Name the file by these wordsTicked: the file is named by your words, then our mark and the width. Unticked: the words are added to the end of the file’s own name.
Type the whole name insteadFor the odd job that needs its own name. Use the original name saves under the name of the file you opened.
57615_full-front_twedit_280w.png
  • 57615_full-frontThe words you typed. A comma starts the next part.
  • _tweditOur mark. It’s been through Graphic Engine and is ready to print.
  • _280wThe print is 280 mm wide.
  • _trace · _flat · _dtgAdded for Trace prep and DTG files, so nobody prints the wrong one.

Production label

This adds a line of words under the design in the saved file, so prints can be told apart on the film. Choose Off, Simple or Full info, and red or yellow. Cut it off after printing. The design itself isn’t touched.

Save

Click Save PNG, at the top or at the bottom of the check list. The file is a 300 dpi PNG at the exact print size, and it lands in your Downloads folder. The tab gets a green tick. Change anything after that and the amber dot comes back, so you know to save again.

Art ready, on the board

When a job came from the Workshop Board and every print file for it has been saved, a bar appears: Mark Art ready on the board or Not yet. It’s your call. Nothing is ticked on the board unless you click it.

7

Change one part or one colour

These are for simple zones. For real retouching, use Photoshop.

Select an area

Open Select and choose Box to drag a box, or Loop to draw around a part freehand. Then open Select again:

Rest untouchedOn already. Whatever you change next (Quick start, the sliders) happens inside the selection only. The rest prints as it opened.
Shadows hereShadows drop out inside the selection only.
Knock out hereClick a colour inside the selection. It’s removed there and nowhere else.
Colour hereWhat prints inside the selection prints in the colour you pick. Select another area to give it its own colour.
ClearBack to changing the whole design.

The three “here” buttons stay in place after you clear the selection. You’ll find them listed under Fine-tune, in Parts, where you can adjust or remove them.

Ink: solid colours

Open Ink in the tool row.

Original coloursThe art prints in its own colours.
One solid colourThe whole design becomes one colour you pick. Handy for a white design lifted off a dark background.
Two or Three solid coloursThe art’s main colours, each one flat. Each has a prints as square: click it to swap that colour for another. Clean cut only.
Allow for DTF black inkOff to start. Our black ink prints as a dark matt grey, never as black as a black tee. Switch this on and the views show that, and on very dark tees the darkest colours are left to the shirt.

With Two solid colours, a third colour in the art joins whichever of the two is nearest. If that’s wrong, use Three.

Crop

Open Crop. Trim to the art cuts away the empty margin. Draw a crop lets you drag your own: Enter applies it, Esc cancels.

8

Fine-tune, only if needed

Click Fine-tune to open the rest of the tools. Leave it shut if the design already looks right. The Quick adjust sliders are the same settings as in here, so try those first.

Every section has a short note, a More link for the longer one, and a Reset link that puts just that section back. Hover over anything for a tip.

Background

Remove the background is for JPGs and screenshots on a plain colour. It clears that colour only where it touches the outside edge, so white inside the design (text, eyes, highlights) stays.

  • Bits of design going too? Lower Tolerance. Background left behind? Raise it.
  • Background shut inside a letter, like the middle of an O, stays. Brush it out with the Eraser in Touch up.

Make see-through areas solid is for AI art. Many AI images look solid but are partly see-through. They print dark on a dark tee and faint on a light one. The check list warns you: “52% of the design is partly see-through”.

  • Tick the box, then choose how the design should look: as it does on White, on Black, or on The shirt colour.
  • Show the see-through areas shows you where they are.
  • If a faint smudge around the design turns into a solid patch, raise Leave out anything fainter than.

Leave it off for real glows, shadows and fades. Those are meant to be soft, and Halftone turns them into dots.

Sharpen & smooth

  • Sharpen (Light, Medium, Strong) brings back crispness in a soft file.
  • Smooth out noise evens out speckle, JPEG blocks and patchy colour, and keeps the edges sharp. Good for small pictures that were enlarged, and AI art. Strong can soften hair or fabric, so check at 1:1.

Brightness & levels

  • Brightness and Contrast work like Photoshop’s. Double-click a slider to put it back to 0. Colours going grey? Tick Keep colour strength.
  • Deepen pale colours is for creams and light tints that print as white. It makes them a little darker and stronger.
  • Calm skin tones is for faces that print too orange or red. It eases skin colours back and leaves everything else alone.
  • Levels: drag the black triangle right and more of the art counts as shadow. Auto has a go for you.
Print a test strip first The screen can’t show how the printer treats pale colours or skin. Under each of those two is a Save a test strip link. Click it, then click a spot on the art. It saves a small strip of that spot at Off, A little and More, labelled, to print and compare. Both settings are still being tuned, so always test before a big run.

Parts

Parts give one piece of the design its own treatment. Click Add a part, then:

  1. Pick it. By tone or colour (Shadows, Midtones, Highlights, Greys, or colours you click on the art), by an area you paint or box, or with Use the selection.
  2. Say what happens to it. Remove, Fade to dots, Own dots, Keep solid, No dots, Main dots, Recolour, or Solid colour.

Show lights up what the part covers. A design can have up to six parts.

Grey skull in red smokePick the greys, then Keep solid or No dots. The smoke gets dots, the skull doesn’t.
Black text on a black teePick the text colour by clicking it on the art, then Recolour to white.
One word must stay solidBox the word with Select, add a part, choose Use the selection, then Keep solid.

Edge

Hard edgeHalftone only. Soft edges print fully solid or are removed, for a crisp outline. Untick it to keep a glow as dots.
Crisp outlinesKeeps lettering and sharp lines clean, not broken up by dots.
Speck clean-upRemoves specks too small to print and fills pinholes. In Clean cut, Specks cleared up to sets how big a speck can be and still go. Raise it when a texture leaves loose dots.
Fade the edgeHalftone only. Breaks the outline into dots over the distance you set. Inward keeps the print the same size. Good for a photo with a hard rectangle edge. The two Outward choices trail dots past the outline, so the print gets bigger. Outward has not been proven in print yet, so test it first.
Trim the edgeShaves the outline in a little. Any colour clears the pale fringe left after a background removal.

Touch up

Three brushes you drag on the preview.

EraserClears stray pixels and leftover background.
PaintFills gaps. Alt-click the art to pick up a colour.
RestoreBrings the original back where you brush.

[ and ] change the brush size. Hold Space to move around. Esc puts the brush down.

The other sections, in one line each

Halftone dotsHow fine the dots are. 30 lpi (lines per inch) is our everyday setting. 35 is finer and may need more care.
ThresholdClean cut only. How solid a soft pixel must be to stay. The same as the Soft edges slider in Quick adjust.
Knock outWhich colour drops out to the shirt, and how close a colour has to be to go with it.
Ink densityHalftone only. Dot limits: Fine, Standard, Extra safe. Standard suits most prints.
Ink colourHow grey our black ink prints. Set once for the printer and leave it.
9

Several designs open at once

Each design opens in its own tab, with its own settings, touch-ups and Undo. Up to 16 can be open. Click + or Open art, or drop several files on the page.

Amber dotNot saved yet, or changed since it was saved.
✓ Green tickSaved, and nothing changed since.
Copy settings to allGives every other open design the set-up of the one on screen: print style, knock-out, levels, ink and shirt colour. Crops and touch-ups stay with each design, and each tab can undo it.
Save allSaves every open design, each as its own PNG.

All tabs: tick and save together

With two or more designs open, All tabs appears at the right of the tab strip. It lists every design with its picture, print size and whether it’s saved.

  1. Tick the designs you want, or Tick all.
  2. Click Save ticked. The tool shows each one in turn and makes its print file.
  3. Two or more come down as one zip in your Downloads folder. One ticked design saves as a plain PNG.

Close the saved ones closes every saved design except the one on screen. Leave the tool alone while it saves. If the design on screen changes part-way, it stops and saves nothing, so nothing is half done.

If the page closes or refreshes, open it again. Your tabs come back as you left them, with Undo. The green ticks don’t, so check your Downloads folder if you’re not sure what was saved.

10

Batch: a whole order

Batch at the top is for many files that share one set-up, like the back names of a team order. Files sit in groups. Each group has one set-up and one print size, and saves as its own folder.

The usual run

  1. Get the files in. An order sent from the Workshop Board arrives already in its groups. For anything else, click New group and add files, or drop files or a zip. A zip with folders makes a group for each folder.
  2. Set each group up. Click a Speed button or choose a Preset on the group. Or click Check or change on a file: one file opens in the editor, you set it up as usual, then click Use for the group in the bar at the top.
  3. Set the print size. Choose how the group is sized, type the mm, and tick Trim each file to its art for names and logos.
  4. Process. Tick the groups and click Process ticked groups. You get one zip with a folder for each group.

How a group is sized

One scale, set by the widest fileThe widest file prints at the size you type and the others follow. Letters come out the same height on every file. Best for names.
Every file the same widthEach file is made exactly that wide.
Every file the same heightEach file is made exactly that tall.

A file that would print bigger than 400 × 500 mm is flagged and left out.

Handy things in Batch

All ticked groupsThe box at the top. A Speed button, Preset or print size chosen here goes to every ticked group at once. Undo takes it back in one step.
Same filesThe tool spots exact copies of a file. Keep one of each unticks the copies so each design is worked out once. Leave them ticked and each folder still gets its copy.
Move ticked to a new groupTick some files in a group and move them out to a group of their own. You can also drag a file from one group to another.
Join ticked groupsPuts the files of every ticked group into one group.
LockWhen a group is right, lock it. It folds to one line and can’t be changed by accident. It still saves with Process ticked groups.
Use for this file onlyIn the editor bar, when one file needs different settings from its group. The file moves to a group of its own.
UndoTakes back the last change in Batch: a move, a join, a size, a removed file.
Send ticked to a sheetWorks the groups out and puts the prints on a gang sheet instead of a zip.

Batch is kept if the page refreshes. The Production label choice at the top is the same one as in Check & save.

Check with Claude

On the Workshop Board’s copy of the tool, the Batch bar has Check with Claude. It works out every ticked group, then has Claude look at each result and flag the ones that need a hand. Nothing is saved or changed by a check.

  • The flagged designs come first, each with a reason and something to try.
  • Open in editor opens that design. Fix it, then choose Use for the group or Use for this file only, and you land back on the check.
  • It opens even when all 16 tabs are in use, so there’s no need to close anything first. A design you only looked at closes by itself when you open the next one. A design you changed stays open in its tab until you choose one of the two Use for buttons, so nothing you did is lost.
  • Fine as it is marks a flag as looked at. Flag it again undoes that.
  • A design you changed shows “Changed since this check”. Check again re-checks just that one.
  • Back to Claude’s check on the Batch bar reopens the last check.

A check sends a small picture of each result and its measurements. No file names, order numbers or customer names are sent. There’s a daily limit, and each check costs a little, so use it for real batches. The results are gone if the page refreshes.

Claude flags, you decide The check is a second pair of eyes, not the final word. Always look the batch over yourself before anything goes to print.

Batch with Claude

For a big order of similar designs, Claude can prepare the whole folder the same way as one design you’ve done by hand, and send back a check sheet. More, then Batch with Claude, has the steps. It’s run from the main Mac.

11

Gang sheet

Sheet at the top packs finished prints onto one sheet of film.

  1. Add prints. Add the open design adds the design in the editor, as it would save now. From Batch, Send ticked to a sheet adds whole groups.
  2. Set how many of each with − and +. The sheet arranges itself.
  3. Click Save sheet. Each sheet is one PNG. Several sheets come down as a zip.
Film width, Gap between prints, Longest sheetIn mm. The tool remembers them on this computer.
Turn prints to save filmLets the tool turn a print on its side when that wastes less film.
Keep each order togetherPrints from the same order sit beside each other.
Check the numbers first The film width, gap and longest sheet the tool starts with are placeholders. Set them to match our printer and film before you trust a sheet. The sheet isn’t kept if the page refreshes, so save it before you leave.
12

Trace prep for Illustrator

Use this when a customer sends a small or fuzzy logo and you want clean vector shapes. Image Trace struggles with fuzzy edges and off-whites. Trace prep fixes the picture first, so the trace comes out clean.

  1. Open the logo. Set the print size to 250 mm or more on the long side. A bigger size traces with smoother curves. Ignore “Upscale needed” here.
  2. In step 2, click Trace prep.
  3. If the logo is on a plain background, open Fine-tune, then Background, and tick Remove the background.
  4. Check the colours in Quick adjust. Auto counts them for you. If it found too many, click the right number under How many colours.
  5. Click Save PNG. The file name ends in _trace.
  6. In Illustrator, place the PNG and run Image Trace. Ask for the number of colours the check list tells you.
  7. Delete the background shape. Done.

Swap a colour

Each colour in the list has a prints as square. Click it to change that colour, for example an off-navy to our navy. Reset puts it back. The same list is in Fine-tune, where you can also click a colour to leave it out so its areas join the nearest colour left.

Why one more colour?

Background for tracing (in Fine-tune) puts a solid colour behind the logo in the saved file, with a small margin. With nothing see-through, Image Trace has no faint edge to turn into stray outlines. That background counts as a colour, so a 3-colour logo needs 4 in Image Trace. The check list always tells you the number.

AutoPicks a colour far from every colour in the logo, often a bright green or yellow. Leave it here unless you have a reason.
Black, White, OwnChoose the background yourself.
OffNo background. The file stays transparent and the name ends in _flat. Ask for the logo’s own number of colours.

The two tidy-up sliders

SmoothingEvens out stair-steps on a low-res logo. Starts at 4. If small text is blobbing, lower it.
Smallest detail keptMelts specks and thin in-between lines into the colour beside them. Starts at 0.5 mm. Raise it for a rough scan.
Check the trace Always check the traced result against the customer’s original. Gradients come out as steps, so Trace prep suits flat logos, not shaded art.
13

Which one do I pick?

The jobClick thisGood to know
Logo or letteringSpeed button Quick clean cutCrisp edge, background gone, trimmed. If the soft part is a glow or drop shadow the customer wants, use Glows & soft shadows.
JPG logo on a white boxClean cut, then Remove the backgroundWhite inside the logo stays. Background left behind? Raise Tolerance in Fine-tune, Background.
Art with dark shading, going on a dark teeClean cut, then Remove shadowsShadows removed up to sets how dark counts as shadow. Loose dots left in a texture? Raise Specks cleared up to.
Photo on a black teeSpeed button Black teeDark backgrounds melt into the shirt with no box. Dim phone photo? Use Dark photo on black.
AI artOpen it and read the check list firstIf it warns the design is partly see-through and it should be solid, tick Make see-through areas solid in Background. Smooth out noise helps washy fills.
Flames, smoke or glowsHalftone, then Fix soft edgesThe Halftone presets have longer fades for flames and smoke. Something in it must stay solid? Add a part and choose Keep solid.
White teeSpeed button White teeWhite in the design becomes the shirt. Art made for dark tees can break up on white.
Coloured teeSet the Shirt colour, then speed button Coloured teeThe safe choice for photos and faces.
One, two or three colour art in the wrong coloursInk in the tool rowOne, Two or Three solid colours, then click a “prints as” square.
Print-ready picture, no dots neededClean cut, then Nothing removed (prep only)Size, tidy, save.
Going on the DTG printerPrint style DTGSolid background, nothing removed.
Names and numbers for a teamBatchOne scale for the group, Trim each file to its art.
Several prints for one run of filmSheetSet how many of each.
Logo to tracePrint style Trace prepSize 250 mm or more. Ask Image Trace for the number of colours the tool gives you.

Not sure? Click a few Speed buttons and Quick starts and watch the After side, or use Try another way to keep two versions. Nothing is lost. Undo takes you back.

14

If something looks wrong

I’ve made a mess of itUndo at the top, or open History and click an earlier step. Under Options in the Tools panel, Revert to as opened goes back to the design as it opened, and Reset to defaults puts the tool’s own settings back.
I can’t find a button this guide mentionsSeveral live in short lists now: Crop, Select, Ink, Other views, Zoom, More and Options. If the Tools panel is missing, click the Tools tab on the right edge.
The badge says “Upscale needed”The file is too small for the size. Click the badge and follow the note: enlarge it in your upscaler, ask for a bigger file, or print it smaller.
A soft glow turned into a solid ringClean cut does that. Choose Halftone, then Fix soft edges, or the Speed button Glows & soft shadows. Already in Halftone? Untick Hard edge in the Edge section.
Parts of the design disappearedThey are close to the shirt colour, so they were knocked out. In Clean cut choose Nothing removed (prep only), or lower Colour cleared near the shirt. In Halftone choose Fix soft edges. Or add a part and choose Keep solid.
The design looks dull or half missing on a dark shirtIt’s probably partly see-through. Read the check list, then tick Make see-through areas solid in Background.
Loose dots or specks in a Clean cut printRaise Specks cleared up to in Quick adjust. Try 1 mm.
Black looks dark grey in the previewAllow for DTF black ink is on, in the Ink list. That’s the honest view: our black ink prints as a dark matt grey.
A pale fringe after removing the backgroundEdge section: Trim the edge, Any colour, a few pixels.
Background colour left inside lettersIt only clears from the outside edge. Use the Eraser in Touch up, or box the letter with Select and use Knock out here.
Check list: the smallest dot is very smallDots that small can wash off. In Ink density click Standard or Extra safe.
Cream prints as white, or faces print too redBrightness & levels: Deepen pale colours or Calm skin tones. Print a test strip first.
My change went on the whole design, not my selectionOpen Select and check Rest untouched is on (pink outline).
I can’t find a presetThe list only shows presets for the print style you’re in.
Save ticked saved nothingThe design on screen changed while it was working. Tick them again, click Save ticked, and leave the tool alone until the file lands.
“Up to 16 designs can be open at once”Open All tabs and click Close the saved ones. Open in editor from Claude’s check is never stopped by this.
Life size isn’t the real sizeOpen Zoom and set Life size up again with a bank card. Each screen needs its own set-up.
I want more roomMore, then Full screen. Esc leaves it. On Chrome or Edge, Install app may also be there: it gives the tool its own window.
Traced logo has wobbly or stepped edgesMake the print size bigger, and raise Smoothing.

Handy keys

  • V step through the views
  • O hold to see the original
  • T flick to Transparent
  • E print edge on or off
  • + − 0 zoom in, out, fit
  • Cmd/Ctrl Z undo, in the editor and in Batch
Written for Graphic Engine version 128, November 2026. Pictures show the tool’s own sample art and made-up test pictures. If a button here doesn’t match what you see, the tool has been updated: trust the tool, and let the owner know so the guide gets fixed.
